headline: Complete streets and Vision Zero: discussion of a possible city ordinance and a road-safety goal of zero deaths and severe injuries.
summary: The commission talked about a complete streets ordinance, which makes streets accessible to all modes of travel, and a possible Vision Zero resolution with a goal of zero deaths and severe injuries by 2045. A meeting with the mayor will be set up to ask about his priorities. Other talk covered beach grass planting in March, a heat study with a UNE fellow, and a dedicated funding trust.
discussion: Complete streets and Vision Zero: Members weighed a complete streets ordinance against a Vision Zero resolution, and pointed to model ordinances from other Maine towns. A meeting with the mayor will be set up to ask about his priorities.

Wild Seed garden upkeep: Members reported that the garden planting is done. They discussed a sign-up for park stewards, a dog-waste sign, and a larger locked storage space near the water access, which public works would need to review.
Beach grass planting: Planting is planned for March, and dune work must happen before March 15. The next step is for council to approve spending funds that are already set aside for this.

Summer fellow heat study: Members discussed applying to the UNE Sustainability Fellowship for a project to map the heat island effect in downtown. The plan includes satellite mapping, ground sensors, census data on vulnerable residents, and a short resident survey, and a member said a decision could come by December 7.

Dedicated funding trust: Members discussed a trust so money is not lost at the end of the fiscal year, which ends June 30. Ideas included a voter referendum and asking the charter commission to set up annual funding.
